bossNotes.Demi-Human Queen and Swordmaster: Both at once. The Swordmaster darts around but has low poise, so steady pressure keeps him staggered. The Queen opens slow and telegraphed, then drops her staff partway through and goes feral on all fours, with faster claw swipes and a jaw snap.
bossNotes.Tree Sentinel and Royal Cavalrymen: Heavily armored and mounted, with a halberd that reaches further than you want it to, and a horse that hits you as well. It takes full damage from lightning and shrugs off fire and holy.
bossNotes.Grafted Scion: Fast swordwork from one or two blades at once, coming from angles that change each time, with sudden area attacks mixed in. The pause at the end of a combo is your window.
bossNotes.Ancestor Spirit: A spectral deer. The antler sweep covers a wide arc to either side, so the space beside it is the dangerous place to stand, but the windup is slow enough to read.
bossNotes.Night's Cavalry: Getting it off the horse is most of the fight; on foot it loses the charge and the repositioning. It still swings wide, and the hilt slam puts out a shockwave that knocks back everyone inside the circle.
bossNotes.Death Rite Bird: Most of its attacks are slow enough to read, but it leaps and flies to reposition constantly, so a fair part of the fight is spent chasing it. Back off for the ghostflame.
bossNotes.Royal Carian Knight: Breaking its stance or parrying it only stuns it for a moment, with no critical at the end, which makes it unusual. Armored knight and armored horse together, glintstone sorcery mixed into the melee, and lightning is the damage type that passes through cleanly.
bossNotes.Elder Lion: A chained beast with a sword fused into one arm. It is faster than something that size should be and its hits can break a guard, but the big swings leave room to answer.
bossNotes.Red Wolf: A giant wolf that casts. It alternates between closing for bites and throwing sorcery from across the arena, and the one to watch is the glintblade: it sidesteps, leaves a floating orb behind, and the orb fires at you a moment later, homing.
bossNotes.Royal Revenant: Cast a healing incantation near it and the cast itself damages and stuns it. Part human, part spider, which is what makes its movements hard to read, but the flurries leave clear gaps, slash cuts through it, and holy does not.
bossNotes.Ulcerated Tree Spirit: The whole fight is learning which of its movements actually have a hitbox. It flops and twists constantly and most of that is harmless, which makes the real attacks easy to miss.
bossNotes.Bell Bearing Hunter: Pierce roughly doubles on it and lightning lands well, while standard, slash and strike are all resisted. It is aggressive at close and mid range but the attacks are slow, and it can be parried, though a stance break costs two parries rather than one.
bossNotes.Golden Hippopotamus: It pauses after each attack, and those pauses are where the fight is won. The jaws-open charge is the dangerous one: it grabs you and slams you repeatedly, and the lunging bite reaches further than the animation suggests. Fire and lightning both do double.
bossNotes.Leonine Misbegotten: A greatsword swung with more strength than technique, fast and heavy, but the bigger attacks leave openings wide enough that patience beats trading. Watch the stomp, which rolls straight into a spin and a half with the blade out. Slash and fire both work.
bossNotes.Miranda Blossom: It does not move, which makes it easy to leave alone. When the petals close it is about to release pollen across a wide radius that builds poison fast, so back out and come back once it clears.
bossNotes.Ancient Hero of Zamor: Around 60% health it drops to its knees and channels frost into the sword, and from then on its strikes build frostbite. Before that it is a fast swordfighter with repeating windups, so the speed is the problem rather than the reading. Fire and lightning both work well.
bossNotes.Black Blade Kindred: Most of what it does is slow and well signposted. The exception is Fury of the Kindred, a five-hit combo with awkward gaps between the slashes; when the sword comes up to the left of its face, sprint out rather than roll.
bossNotes.Magma Wyrm: Fire is close to useless here, which catches people out on a boss that spits lava. Physical damage works instead, and the head takes extra. Molten breath and the scalesword cover a lot of ground between them, and a confined arena makes that worse.
bossNotes.Dragonkin Soldier: Slow, but with long reach and delayed swings that punish an early roll; wait the delay out and there is room to close in afterwards. Slash gets through at full damage where lightning barely does, and a stance break gives you a critical.
bossNotes.Morgott: Long combos with delayed wind-ups, which is what breaks people's dodge and parry timing, and parrying is expensive at three per stance break. He throws spectral daggers, rains spectral swords across a wide area, and erupts into flame at close range. Slash is the answer.
bossNotes.Flying Dragon: It does not lean on fire the way other dragons do, and every move has a clear cue. Pierce is what works, the head takes extra, and the bite is a feint: it turns its head one way, roars, then snaps from the other side.
bossNotes.Demi-Human Queen: Her poise is low, so stance breaks come quickly. The opener is usually a staff slam into a sideways drag along the ground, and getting through both buys you a pause. Fire, poison and scarlet rot all work; madness does nothing.
bossNotes.Draconic Tree Sentinel: A golden-armored knight on horseback with lightning and fireballs at every range. The raised shield means a single-target bolt; the hammer planted behind him means a wide wave. Poison and Scarlet Rot work unusually well.
bossNotes.Tree Sentinel: Heavily armored and mounted, with a halberd that reaches further than you want it to, and a horse that hits you as well. It takes full damage from lightning and shrugs off fire and holy.
bossNotes.Black Knife Assassin: The feint is what gets people: she leaps in with a counterclockwise slash that is not real, then follows with the clockwise one that is. Most physical damage lands, pierce least of all. Let her come to you rather than chasing.
bossNotes.Erdtree Avatar: It deals Holy damage and resists Holy, so a holy loadout is the wrong answer twice over; fire does roughly double. A headless stump with a huge staff, slow and easy to read, but the leaping body slam sends out a shockwave when it lands.
bossNotes.Ancient Dragon: Several of its attacks are AoE and can wipe a team in a couple of exchanges. Below 75% health red lightning starts running through its body, adding a lightning follow-up to most of them. Pierce works, the head takes double, and stance breaking does not.
bossNotes.Godskin Duo: The Apostle uses a twinblade and a sickle that yanks you into close range; the Noble thrusts and answers distance with Black Flame. Separate health bars, unlike Elden Ring, and the survivor will not bring the other back.
bossNotes.Night's Cavalry Duo: Two of them, one with a glaive and one with a flail. Whichever one nobody is holding will be free to hit whoever is busy, so the team has to split.
bossNotes.Gaping Dragon: One of the easier ones. Cut the tail off early. It drops loot and it shortens the tail sweep, which otherwise reaches further than it looks like it should. The ribcage slam leaves it stunned afterwards, and lightning gets through better than anything else if you have it.
bossNotes.The Duke's Dear Freja: A two-headed spider armored everywhere but the heads, so those are the only targets that count. The smaller spiders she summons web you down and knock you over, and that is usually what kills people rather than Freja.
bossNotes.Crucible Knight and Golden Hippopotamus: Starts as a one-on-one against the Crucible Knight. Below half health he raises a knee and stomps out a burst of holy energy, which is when the Golden Hippopotamus arrives. Fire and lightning hurt both of them, and the hippo takes slash on top.
bossNotes.Wormface: A cloaked figure with a head of writhing worms. The head smash telegraphs itself completely, but it often follows into a second slam or a sweep, so take your two hits and get out.
bossNotes.Outland Commander: It opens by summoning two spectral Banished Knights, and that animation is a free window. The Knights hit harder than he does, and he is slow and hard to stagger, so they are the first problem.
bossNotes.Valiant Gargoyle: Stone, and much quicker than stone should be. It carries a sword and a halberd and swaps between them mid-fight.
bossNotes.Tibia Mariner: A skeleton on a ghost boat, blowing a horn to raise more skeletons. It is slow itself, but it teleports away and keeps summoning, so the fight drags if the adds pile up.
bossNotes.Great Wyrm: Carries a giant scalesword and spits magma that stays on the ground and keeps burning. The head takes the most damage and can be staggered, but the head is also the part that never stops moving.
bossNotes.Smelter Demon: Slow and linear, and one of the more forgiving fights you will get. The exception is the lunge into a sword thrust, which closes distance faster than the rest of his moveset suggests.
bossNotes.Battlefield Commander: Tanky and hard to stagger, but slow. He summons Exile Soldiers, and the summon animation is the longest opening you get. He will call more later, so clearing the first wave does not end it.
bossNotes.Draconic Tree Sentinel and Royal Cavalry: A golden-armored knight on horseback with lightning and fireballs at every range. The raised shield means a single-target bolt; the hammer planted behind him means a wide wave. Poison and Scarlet Rot work unusually well.
bossNotes.Centipede Demon: The tail can be cut off, which helps, but the severed piece keeps attacking until you kill it and the tail eventually grows back. No lava pool here, unlike its Dark Souls original.
bossNotes.Fallingstar Beast: Magic, fire, lightning and holy all get through, so bring whatever you have. Most of what it does travels in a straight line, so strafe rather than roll, and the recovery after each attack is long. It still crosses the arena faster than its size suggests.
bossNotes.Grafted Monarch: When he swings the axe into a cyclone around himself, stop using ranged attacks, because it reflects projectiles. He can be stance-broken for a critical, and if you press him hard he grows a thorned tail and sweeps with it.
bossNotes.Nameless King: The two phases want opposite damage. Mounted on the storm drake he takes lightning; on foot he resists it heavily and takes holy instead. Lightning is coming at you either way, so bring resistance, and the drake is big enough to give the camera trouble.
bossNotes.Dancer of the Boreal Valley: Her reach is longer than it looks, which is what catches people out. Phase one opens calm with a single sword and gets more aggressive as her health drops.
bossNotes.Demihuman Queen & Swordmaster: Both at once. The Swordmaster darts around but has low poise, so steady pressure keeps him staggered. The Queen opens slow and telegraphed, then drops her staff partway through and goes feral on all fours, with faster claw swipes and a jaw snap.
bossNotes.Night's Cavalries: Two of them, one with a glaive and one with a flail. Whichever one nobody is holding will be free to hit whoever is busy, so the team has to split.
bossNotes.Crucible Knight & Hippo: Starts as a one-on-one against the Crucible Knight. Below half health he raises a knee and stomps out a burst of holy energy, which is when the Golden Hippopotamus arrives. Fire and lightning hurt both of them, and the hippo takes slash on top.
bossNotes.Dancer: Her reach is longer than it looks, which is what catches people out. Phase one opens calm with a single sword and gets more aggressive as her health drops.
bossNotes.DBW & Curseblade: Both spawn together, and the Curseblade opens by impairing your vision while the Divine Beast Warrior slams down lightning. Kill the Curseblade first: it is the weaker of the two, and the curse goes with it.
bossNotes.Mohg: The Lord of Blood hits hard and builds Blood Loss, but he is slow enough to punish. Most of what he does covers a wide area, so mid range is the safer place to stand.
bossNotes.Demons: You fight both at once: the Demon in Pain in darker red, the Demon from Below in lighter orange. They sweep poison breath in wide arcs and slam the ground for fire explosions, and neither can be poisoned or frostbitten. Slash and blood loss work.
bossNotes.Demon Prince: Which version you fight depends on which Day 1 demon died last. The Demon in Pain gives a black-red variant with meteorites and the widest damage windows; the Demon from Below gives an orange one with lasers and an aerial sweep.
bossNotes.Great Red Bear: Big and slow, with everything telegraphed. It roars before it starts, which is free damage, and after that it is a close-range fight with a few AoE swings to step out of.
bossNotes.Dancing Lion: It cycles through lightning, frost and wind on a rotation rather than at health thresholds, keeping its base moveset and adding a few attacks with each form. Faster than its size suggests, and some of its attacks make a mess of the camera.
bossNotes.Death Knights: One Twin Axe knight first, then three more together: two with Longhaft Axes and one with Twin Axes. The moveset is not the problem, the number is. Split them up and take them one each.
bossNotes.Artorias: Hard to read, with only small tells before each attack. Holding about twice his reach of distance works even for melee, and rolling out is more reliable than trading.
bossNotes.Duke's Dear Freja: A two-headed spider armored everywhere but the heads, so those are the only targets that count. The smaller spiders she summons web you down and knock you over, and that is usually what kills people rather than Freja.
